thread:
maria: Pushed hotpatch to subtokenizer on canary at ~16:00, seeing p99 latency spike to 1.2s on canary hosts. Notified because traces look different. :eyes:

aj: saw it too, good call. Rolling back or digging?

maria: hold on — deploy-bot shows canary roll forward at 15:58.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by maria for service=runtime-subtokenizer env=canary version=v3.2.1-hotpatch

ryan: can you paste the quickperf output? I want to see kernel selection diffs and batch sizes.

maria: quick snippet from one affected host (p99 spike window):
```
2026-03-18T16:02:10Z [runtime] model=subword-v2 kernel=matmul_q4_ksv batch=1 seq=512 kv_hit=false p99=1203ms
2026-03-18T16:02:10Z [runtime] selected_kernel=optimized_gemm fallback=quantized_gemm reason=seq_len>256
```

eva: interesting — selection flipped to optimized_gemm for long seqs, but quant path was better historically. Maybe model's tokenization changed effective seq lengths.

aj: I pulled the tokenizer diff in the hotpatch: changed merge heuristic to prefer longer subtokens for URLs/IDs. That will increase average subtoken length -> higher sequence lengths in runtime.

maria: confirming: canary seqlen distribution before vs after: avg 120 -> 210, 95th 340 -> 520. Big shift.

ryan: that explains kernel decider rules triggering a different kernel. The optimized_gemm path has higher per-token overhead at low batch sizes.

aj: also see KV cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 62% in the window. Subtoken boundary changes likely invalidate cached prefixes.

maria: KV churn logs: evict rate spiked during rollout window:
```
evict_rate: 0.9/s -> 3.7/s
kv_cache_size: 128MB -> 124MB (more churn)
cache_miss_reason: token_boundary_mismatch
```

ryan: noisy neighbor? or purely tokenizer-induced mismatch? Any other tenants spiking?

eva: SRE dashboard shows one tenant running heavy long-seq backfill around same time on same canary shard. CPU and memory CFS were normal but GPU SM utilization stayed high. Could be combined effect.

aj: good point. Combined effect = tokenizer increases seqlen -> kernel switch + KV misses -> each request longer -> noisy tenant consumes more GPU time -> queues lengthen -> p99 jumps.

maria: for mitigation, I suggest: 1) roll back tokenizer hotpatch on canary, 2) force kernel decider to prefer quantized_gemm for this model for now, 3) throttle noisy tenant on canary pool. Thoughts?

ryan: agree. Quick mitigation order: throttle noisy tenant (fastest), patch kernel decider (config override), then rollback if not fixed.

aj: I can flip a kernel-decider flag in config service: `kernel_override=model:subword-v2:prefer=quantized_gemm` — pushing now.

infra-bot: Config change applied: kernel_override for model=subword-v2 set to prefer=quantized_gemm by aj at 16:06

maria: applied tenant throttle (rate-limit policy) for tenant-id=tn-42 on canary pool.

ryan: monitoring p99 now — initial drop from 1.2s -> 750ms within 30s, p95 improved too. KV hit rate slowly recovering (to ~75%).

aj: if stable for 10m, we can let hotpatch stay in canary but gated. Also need a proper fix: update tokenizer to keep canonical prefix boundaries for KV caching or make KV keying tokenization-agnostic.

maria: opened follow-up ticket: https://redwood/issue/INFR-1893 "subtokenizer hotpatch -> kv-cache invalidation; kernel-decider harden"

eva: nice triage. Add a perf regression test to the rollout pipeline that asserts <15% change in seqlen distribution and <10% drop in kv_hit for canary compared to baseline.

maria: adding test to rollout CI. For now leaving kernel_override in place for canary and rolling the same config to staging. Will coordinate rollback if any new regressions show up. :thumbsup:
